newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt spreads flat amid Treasury dip.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt spreads flat amid Treasury dip.

text.p: U.S. corporate bond spreads were unchanged in moderate trade as the Treasury market dealt with a wave of selling following stronger than expected housing data, dealers said.
A handful of traders reported a rise in selling from accounts amid growing new corporate supply, but they also stressed sell lists were met with aggressive bidding.

"New issues have taken away some of the thunder in the market and we've seen a few more bid lists today than actual buy inquiries," said a trader at a New York retail firm. "Spreads have pretty much held in there, though."

Corporate debt investors were said to buy on dips after a 9.2 percent jump in housing starts for November sent the yield on the Treasury long bond to its highest level since October 30, traders said. Analysts had expected the data to reflect little change in the level of housing starts.

New issues received the bulk of attention, however, and sources pointed to the $400 million upsizing of Rite Aid Corp's multi-tranche debt offering as evidence of still-strong demand for paper heading into year-end.
The Rite Aid issue is now $1.0 billion and is expected to be priced by lead manager Goldman, Sachs & Co on Tuesday.
Elsewhere, Citicorp issued $300 million in capital securities due 2027 to yield 120 basis points over the Treasury curve via a Merrill Lynch & Co Inc led syndicate.
One trader away from the deal said the securities were well-bid despite what some considered too-tight spreads. Much of the deal was done through "some pretty aggressive swapping," the trader added.
Turning to the high-yield market, dealers said prices were marginally lower amid softness in Treasuries. New issues traded at premiums but were not immune to 1/4 point drops in the broad marketplace.
In recent issuance, Heartland Wireless Communications Inc's $125 million par 14 percent senior notes due 2004 were bid at 102 near mid-session.
BT Securities Corp priced the deal late on Monday.

Bankrupt Anchor Glass Container Corp debt has seen buyers for the past couple of days, according to one trader. Anchor's 10-1/4 percent debt due 2002 traded at a 77 bid on Tuesday, unchanged from Monday's close.
The benchmark U.S. Treasury bond was quoted down 17/32 to yield 6.67 percent at 1400 EST/1900 GMT.
